name: Konyanka Maninka
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: [Davydov, p. 170:] Большинство идиомов манден имеет две базовые тоновые схемы слов. […] Как видно из таблицы, высокотоновым словам манинка-мори соответствуют в конья слова с низким тоном, а словам манинка-мори, имеющим низкий тон, в конья соответствуют слова с высоким тоном. Можно сказать, что тоны в конья по сравнению с манинка-мори являются инвертированными. [Vydrin, p. 34:] У д а р е н и е в большинстве М.я. отсутствует. Там, где оно может быть выделено (в частности, бамана), его функциональная нагрузка невелика.
new_statements.translation: [Davydov, p. 170:] Most Manding idioms have two basic word tone schemes. [...] As the table shows, high-tone words of Maninka-Mori correspond in Konya to words with low tone, and Maninka-Mori words that have low tone correspond in Konya to words with high tone. One can say that the tones of Konya, compared with Maninka-Mori, are inverted. [Vydrin, p. 34:] Stress is absent in most Mande languages. Where it can be identified (in particular in Bamana), its functional load is small.
new_statements.citation: Davydov, A. V. 2017. Manden dialekty Gvinei. In: V. F. Vydrin, Ju. V. Mazurova, A. A. Kibrik & E. B. Markus (eds), Jazyki mira: Jazyki mande, 164-171 (p. 170). St Petersburg: Nestor-Istorija; with Vydrin, V. F. 2017. Mande jazyki, same volume, p. 34 (family-level).
new_statements.locator: Davydov p. 170 (PDF p. 170), tone-class table and following paragraph; Vydrin p. 34 (PDF p. 34), paragraph 'Ударение'
new_statements.rule_in_words: Konyanka (Konya) is a lexical-tone language of the Manding type: every word belongs to one of two tone classes (H or L, realised over the whole word, e.g. bá 'goat', bà 'mother', mɔ́ɔ̀ 'person', bàlà 'xylophone'), and its classes are the mirror image of those of Maninka-Mori (tonal inversion). No source states any word-stress rule for Konyanka; the only stress remark is the family-level one that stress is absent in most Mande languages.
new_statements.exceptions: Davydov p. 170: transitional lects between Maninka and Konya have partially inverted tone schemes and are poorly documented. Vydrin p. 34: stress is identifiable in some Mande languages (Bamana) but with small functional load.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tone classes of citation forms from Davydov's dialect questionnaire; the stress remark is about the Mande family as a whole, not Konyanka specifically. Vydrin p. 19 states explicitly that the available data on Konya are limited to Davydov's questionnaire.
new_statements.identity_note: The 2017 sources describe 'Konya' (конья, коньянка) of Beyla/Kerouane prefectures (Guinea) with sub-lects gbeeka, gbasando, woroduu, karagba, from Davydov's dialect questionnaire; hh.bib maps Davydov's 'Kon'ya i tyagoteyushchie k nemu govory' to mku = kony1250. Do not confuse with Manya (many1261, mzj; Macenta/Liberia), the sister lect of the same Konya-Manya sub-continuum, described by Cutler & Dwyer 1981 and Heydorn 1943-50; nor with Maninka-Mori/Kankan Maninka (east2426, emk), relative to which Konya tones are inverted.

sources.citation: Vydrin, V. F. 2017. Mande jazyki [Mande languages] (family overview). In: Vydrin et al. (eds), Jazyki mira: Jazyki mande, 16-45 (Konya pp. 18-19, prosody p. 34). St Petersburg: Nestor-Istorija.
sources.note: p. 34 (family-level): 'Ударение в большинстве М.я. отсутствует. Там, где оно может быть выделено (в частности, бамана), его функциональная нагрузка невелика.' pp. 18-19 on Konya: close to Guinean Maninka in lexicon/grammar, differs in segmental phonetics and by tonal inversion; 'the available data on Konya are limited to A. V. Davydov's dialect questionnaire'. No Konya-specific stress statement.

sources.citation: Pioneer Bible Translators. 2003. Maninka Sentence Repetition Test survey report: an investigation into the degree of bilingualism proficiency between Maninka of Kankan and Malinke, Kuranko, Sankaran, Konyanka as well as other dialects of Maninka. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2003-016, 51 pp.
sources.note: Sociolinguistic only (SRT bilingualism; Konyanka population 216,036; recommends Konya be treated as a separate ethnolinguistic group). 'Accent' occurs only in the SRT scoring rubric. Cites unpublished PBT-Guinea 1995 'Konyanka and Manya Survey Report'.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 record mku (Konyanka Maninka; member of macrolanguage Mandingo)

Davydov, A. V. 2017. Manden dialekty Gvinei [Manding dialects of Guinea]. In: V. F. Vydrin, Ju. V. Mazurova, A. A. Kibrik & E. B. Markus (eds), Jazyki mira: Jazyki mande, 164-171. St Petersburg: Nestor-Istorija.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent (grepped 'ударен'/'акцент' across the chapter). Konya is characterised by tone: p. 166 Konya(+Manya) sub-continuum has 'inverted tone schemes'; p. 170 two basic word tone schemes, table Maninka-Mori vs Konya (bà/bá 'goat', bá/bà 'mother', mɔ̀ɔ́/mɔ́ɔ̀ 'person', bálá/bàlà 'xylophone'), 'tones in Konya are inverted relative to Maninka-Mori'. Data = Davydov's own dialect questionnaire.

sources.citation: Sullivan, Terrence D. 2004. A preliminary report of existing information on the Manding languages of West Africa: summary and suggestions for future research. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2004-005, 34 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 4.5 'Konyanka' (p. 14): 'In Guinea, in the region of Beyla to the Ivory Coast Border, the Konyanka dialect of Manding is known... I have not been able to find much information on this dialect of Manding.' 'Tone systems' (p. 24) is family-level: terrace tone, lexical contrast, tonal inversion in Odienne Dyula (Braconnier 1982).

sources.citation: Cutler, Sue A. & David J. Dwyer. 1981. Maniyaka: A Reference Handbook of Phonetics, Grammar, Lexicon and Learning Procedures. East Lansing: MSU African Studies Center (Peace Corps). ERIC ED247767.
sources.note: Describes Manya (Liberian Mandingo, many1261), not Konyanka: two tones HIGH/LOW (p. 50), syllable-timed (p. 51); p. 166 family-level 'While stress is generally non-contrastive in Mande it is generally distinctive. In Kpelle, it falls on the first high-toned syllable...' -- Kpelle rule only, nothing for Manya or Konya.
